chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who has sores and wounds and becomes junub, so he said:
“There is no harm in his performing tayammum and not performing ghusl.”

key_terms.الْقُرُوحُ: sores or ulcers affecting the body
key_terms.فَيُجْنِبُ: he enters the state of janabah
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمَ: he performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلَ: he performs ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for tayammum instead of ghusl for a junub person with wounds or sores?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person afflicted with sores and wounds who enters the state of janabah. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits tayammum in place of ghusl when using water would be problematic due to bodily injury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.217 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a man who has sores and wounds and becomes junub (ritually impure due to sexual discharge).
Imam (as) said:
'There is no harm if he performs tayammum and does not make ghusl (ritual bath).'
